title: Beef Rendang
description: Beef simmered in coconut milk and spice paste until the liquid goes, then fried in the oil that separates out. The last twenty minutes are where it stops being a curry.
notes: Stop early and you have a wet rendang, which is a real dish but a different one. Dry rendang keeps for days unrefrigerated, which is what it was for.

steps.text: Blend the shallots, garlic, soaked dried red chillies, galangal, ginger, and coriander into a smooth paste with a splash of water.
Fry the paste in a wide heavy pot until it darkens and smells sweet rather than raw.
steps.tip: A wide pot, not a deep one. The whole method depends on evaporation.

steps.text: Add the beef chuck and turn it through the paste until sealed.
Pour in the coconut milk and add the lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, turmeric leaves, palm sugar, and salt.
steps.tip: Do not cover the pot at any point.

steps.text: Simmer uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the sauce has reduced to a thick gravy.
Keep going. The oil will split out and the gravy will turn dark brown — now stir constantly so the beef fries in it rather than catching.
steps.tip: This is the actual cooking. The colour goes from tan to near-black and the smell changes completely.

steps.text: Serve once the beef is coated in dark paste and there is no liquid left in the pot.
